title: CLO 2024 Academic Month  Practical Reform of the Apparel Professional Curriculum System Based on CLO3D
description: CLO Academic Month 2024 Review! A conversation with Teacher Luo Shunhua from Shandong University of Art & Design, exploring the process of integrating 3D clothing technology into fashion major courses, from the initial attempts to gradually expanding the course content and scope of reform, as well as practical cases and reflections during the curriculum reform.

chunks.content: # Practical Reform of the Apparel Professional Curriculum System Based on CLO3D This document details the integration and reform of the apparel professional curriculum system using CLO3D software. It covers the background and rationale for curriculum changes, technical implementations, course structures, case studies, and future directions involving digital technologies such as 3D scanning, fabric scanning, Blender software, and artificial intelligence (AI). --- ## Introduction to the School and Curriculum Reform Background This section explains the context of the apparel professional curriculum reform, focusing on the adoption of CLO3D software and digital technologies to align with industry trends in intelligent, functional, and digital fashion development. - The school is a public art institution with a strong focus on design, emphasizing innovation and implementation in clothing education. - The curriculum integrates traditional German methods, including traditional clothing culture, craftsmanship, pattern making, cultural patterns, and clothing history as core modules. - The training goal emphasizes creative application and design talent by combining science, humanities, art, and practical skills. - The reform started in 2017, driven by the digital transformation in the fashion industry. - CLO3D was first encountered as a promising technology during studies at Donghua University in 2010 and formally introduced into the curriculum around 2019. --- ## Development of the Digital Lab and Technology Infrastructure This section outlines the establishment of a digital lab and introduction of key digital tools essential for the curriculum reform. - In 2016, the school proposed building a digital lab dedicated to apparel. - By 2019, with support from CLO3D and the Shanghai Information Department, the apparel digital lab was established, introducing CLO3D software. - Additional equipment introduced: - 3D human body scanning systems. - Fabric scanning machine (introduced in 2020). - By 2022, the lab supported: - Human body measurement and 3D model construction. - Clothing design and pattern adjustment. - Fabric scanning and textile production. - Demonstrations of interactive clothing design processes. - A current limitation is the lack of accurate physical performance testing for scanned fabrics; the lab is working to resolve this mismatch within 1-2 years. --- ## Curriculum System Reform and Course Structure This section describes the transition from single-course offerings to an integrated course system leveraging CLO3D and related software. - Initial use of CLO3D started as a single course in 2020 called "Clothing Design Technology." - Gradual expansion into multiple courses integrating CLO3D for product development and technical training. - Since last year, exploration of combining CLO3D with Blender software to enable virtual dynamic displays and animation. - The course system now includes: - Traditional floating board structure teaching methods combined with CLO3D technology. - A course titled "Fuzhang Three-dimensional Virtual Representation" teaching CLO3D basics to advanced skills. - CLO3D is employed across specialties such as clothing design, human resources, and engineering. - The reform aims to integrate 3D software into traditional German class groups focusing on patterns, colors, and materials to modernize the curriculum.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Academic Month  Practical Reform of the Apparel Professional Curriculum System Based on CLO3D
chunks.content: - Since last year, exploration of combining CLO3D with Blender software to enable virtual dynamic displays and animation. - The course system now includes: - Traditional floating board structure teaching methods combined with CLO3D technology. - A course titled "Fuzhang Three-dimensional Virtual Representation" teaching CLO3D basics to advanced skills. - CLO3D is employed across specialties such as clothing design, human resources, and engineering. - The reform aims to integrate 3D software into traditional German class groups focusing on patterns, colors, and materials to modernize the curriculum. --- ## Case Studies: Practical Applications of CLO3D in Courses This section presents specific course examples showcasing how CLO3D and related technologies are used in practice. ### 1. Clothing and Human Resources Engineering Course - Focuses on software technology training starting from basic garment types: shirts, pants, trousers. - Students progress to structural design and 3D presentations of their designs. - Targeted mainly at first-year students to establish early mastery of software tools. - Encourages independent learning with classroom discussions supporting self-study. ### 2. 3D Human Scanning and Digital Modeling Course - In cooperation with the school's numerical academy and digital animation specialty. - Students design 3D human scan methods, collect and process 3D body models. - Models undergo verification and fitting adjustments. - Customized design plans are created for one-on-one projects. - Students scan chosen fabric materials using the fabric scanner, generating multiple file formats including line drawings and 3D representations. - Physical parameters of fabrics are measured separately but currently only serve as general reference data. - Digital costume production includes creating virtual embroidery shows using Blender in collaboration with the digital academy. - Example project: An autumn/winter coat collection themed on pinstripes, allowing creative freedom in color and material expression. ### 3. Costume Paper Pattern Class - Focuses on understanding the relationship between 2D flat patterns and 3D garment forms. - Utilizes traditional Fuzi board structure, including restoration and reconstruction efforts. - Digital conversion of paper patterns through AI integration to create fabric-compatible digital patterns. - Aims to bridge traditional pattern-making with modern digital technologies. ### 4. Innovation Projects and Competitions - Students apply digital technologies including CLO3D and Macro 3D software in innovation projects. - Example: A survival show concept using traditional Shandong craftsmanship combined with modern fashion styles. - Students employ traditional embroidery techniques (e.g., Lu Jing patterns) in 3D digital redesign. - Participation in competitions such as the three-dimensional digital redesign of traditional fashion led to nominations and valuable design insights. ### 5. Industry Collaboration Project - Cooperation with a Tai’an-based functional clothing company specializing in motorbike suits. - Joint development of a children’s dragonfly suit incorporating oversized design, traditional cultural elements, and protective functions. - Highlights challenges of balancing design freedom with functional and cultural requirements. ### 6. Student Projects and Research Integration - Example: A student-designed high-temperature yoga suit using CLO3D for shape simulation and dynamic verification.

Industry Collaboration Project - Cooperation with a Tai’an-based functional clothing company specializing in motorbike suits. - Joint development of a children’s dragonfly suit incorporating oversized design, traditional cultural elements, and protective functions. - Highlights challenges of balancing design freedom with functional and cultural requirements. ### 6. Student Projects and Research Integration - Example: A student-designed high-temperature yoga suit using CLO3D for shape simulation and dynamic verification. - The project included static and magnetic shape analysis, leading to a research paper potentially publishable in a core journal. - Courses integrate CLO3D with other software, such as Blender, for digital male model animation and virtual costume presentations. --- ## Future Directions and Curriculum Reform Considerations This section discusses strategic thinking on further integration of digital technologies, AI, and ecosystem building for apparel education. ### 1. Building a 3D Resource Library and Sharing Platform - Aim to create a comprehensive, ecosystem-like database of 3D models, course materials, and teaching resources. - Envisioned as a mobile app or platform enabling resource sharing among educators and students. - Expected to significantly improve teaching efficiency and knowledge retention. ### 2. Integration of CLO3D with Other Digital Software - Combining CLO3D with Blender enables virtual dynamic display and video scene integration. - Potential to replace physical models with fully virtual presentations, streamlining production and display. - Already applied in flat broadcast-style clothing presentations with AI-assisted scene fusion. ### 3. Artificial Intelligence Generation (AIGX) in Design - Future courses will focus on integrating AIGX technologies capable of generating images, videos, and content. - AI will enhance design efficiency and compensate for skill gaps, especially for engineering students with weaker traditional drawing skills. - Emphasis on fostering design thinking and methods, encouraging student-driven exploration and independent learning. - AI and project-guided courses are expected to become central to the curriculum, combining business and creative projects. --- ## Summary The reform of the apparel professional curriculum system centers on adopting CLO3D and complementary digital technologies to modernize apparel education. This includes establishing digital labs with 3D human and fabric scanning, integrating 3D software with traditional pattern-making methods, encouraging innovation through competitions, collaborating with industry partners, and embracing AI-driven design tools. Future efforts aim to build shared digital resource platforms and fully virtualize design and presentation processes to enhance teaching effectiveness and student capabilities in the digital fashion era.

The reform aims to integrate 3D software into traditional German class groups focusing on patterns, colors, and materials to modernize the curriculum. --- ## Case Studies: Practical Applications of CLO3D in Courses This section presents specific course examples showcasing how CLO3D and related technologies are used in practice. ### 1. Clothing and Human Resources Engineering Course - Focuses on software technology training starting from basic garment types: shirts, pants, trousers. - Students progress to structural design and 3D presentations of their designs. - Targeted mainly at first-year students to establish early mastery of software tools. - Encourages independent learning with classroom discussions supporting self-study. ### 2. 3D Human Scanning and Digital Modeling Course - In cooperation with the school's numerical academy and digital animation specialty. - Students design 3D human scan methods, collect and process 3D body models. - Models undergo verification and fitting adjustments. - Customized design plans are created for one-on-one projects. - Students scan chosen fabric materials using the fabric scanner, generating multiple file formats including line drawings and 3D representations. - Physical parameters of fabrics are measured separately but currently only serve as general reference data. - Digital costume production includes creating virtual embroidery shows using Blender in collaboration with the digital academy. - Example project: An autumn/winter coat collection themed on pinstripes, allowing creative freedom in color and material expression. ### 3. Costume Paper Pattern Class - Focuses on understanding the relationship between 2D flat patterns and 3D garment forms. - Utilizes traditional Fuzi board structure, including restoration and reconstruction efforts. - Digital conversion of paper patterns through AI integration to create fabric-compatible digital patterns. - Aims to bridge traditional pattern-making with modern digital technologies. ### 4. Innovation Projects and Competitions - Students apply digital technologies including CLO3D and Macro 3D software in innovation projects. - Example: A survival show concept using traditional Shandong craftsmanship combined with modern fashion styles. - Students employ traditional embroidery techniques (e.g., Lu Jing patterns) in 3D digital redesign. - Participation in competitions such as the three-dimensional digital redesign of traditional fashion led to nominations and valuable design insights. ### 5. Industry Collaboration Project - Cooperation with a Tai’an-based functional clothing company specializing in motorbike suits. - Joint development of a children’s dragonfly suit incorporating oversized design, traditional cultural elements, and protective functions. - Highlights challenges of balancing design freedom with functional and cultural requirements. ### 6. Student Projects and Research Integration - Example: A student-designed high-temperature yoga suit using CLO3D for shape simulation and dynamic verification. - The project included static and magnetic shape analysis, leading to a research paper potentially publishable in a core journal. - Courses integrate CLO3D with other software, such as Blender, for digital male model animation and virtual costume presentations. --- ## Future Directions and Curriculum Reform Considerations This section discusses strategic thinking on further integration of digital technologies, AI, and ecosystem building for apparel education. ### 1. Building a 3D Resource Library and Sharing Platform - Aim to create a comprehensive, ecosystem-like database of 3D models, course materials, and teaching resources. - Envisioned as a mobile app or platform enabling resource sharing among educators and students. - Expected to significantly improve teaching efficiency and knowledge retention. ### 2. Integration of CLO3D with Other Digital Software - Combining CLO3D with Blender enables virtual dynamic display and video scene integration. - Potential to replace physical models with fully virtual presentations, streamlining production and display. - Already applied in flat broadcast-style clothing presentations with AI-assisted scene fusion. ### 3. Artificial Intelligence Generation (AIGX) in Design - Future courses will focus on integrating AIGX technologies capable of generating images, videos, and content. - AI will enhance design efficiency and compensate for skill gaps, especially for engineering students with weaker traditional drawing skills. - Emphasis on fostering design thinking and methods, encouraging student-driven exploration and independent learning. - AI and project-guided courses are expected to become central to the curriculum, combining business and creative projects. --- ## Summary The reform of the apparel professional curriculum system centers on adopting CLO3D and complementary digital technologies to modernize apparel education. This includes establishing digital labs with 3D human and fabric scanning, integrating 3D software with traditional pattern-making methods, encouraging innovation through competitions, collaborating with industry partners, and embracing AI-driven design tools. Future efforts aim to build shared digital resource platforms and fully virtualize design and presentation processes to enhance teaching effectiveness and student capabilities in the digital fashion era.
